policy.purpose: Phase-3 owner ADRs freeze the public contract of each capability before any implementation or dependency exit may start. An ADR is a decision record, not an implementation licence.
policy.no_loss_rule: No ADR may authorize removal or narrowing of an accepted public API, generic extension point, Cargo feature, binary, accepted format, wire protocol, platform cell, diagnostic, third-party integration, or documented user journey. Additive redesign is permitted; erasure is not.
policy.keep_default: When a complete owned replacement is disproportionate or its parity is unproven, the required terminal decision is KEEP_UNTIL_PARITY with cutover_state KEEP_INCUMBENT.
policy.no_compatibility_shims: Asupersync is pre-1.0 with no external users to protect. Preserved surfaces stay because the capability is real, not because a deprecated alias is kept alive. ADRs may not introduce compatibility shims or wrapper facades for deprecated APIs.
policy.authority_rule: An ADR carries decision authority only for the capability IDs mapped to its bead by bead_mapping_rules in the capability registry. Cross-cutting capability mentions are compatibility obligations, never primary evidence ownership.
policy.evidence_rule: Every ADR names the exact unit-test owner, no-mock E2E owner, and stable scenario IDs that must be green before its capability may cut over. Naming planned evidence is not the same as having run it.
policy.truthful_baseline_rule: An ADR must record the capability as it actually is at claim time, including gaps, quarantined surfaces, and dead code paths. Freezing an aspirational surface is a defect; known gaps are recorded so they cannot silently widen.
policy.aggregate_rule: asupersync-dep-p3-api-adrs-h3jspm.13 may not close while any roster row is PENDING or any resolved row carries an UNKNOWN capability, format, feature, platform, interoperability, or user-journey field.

surface_state_meanings.SHIPPED_OWNED: Implemented in asupersync's own code and reachable in a production build.
surface_state_meanings.SHIPPED_VIA_DEPENDENCY: Reachable in production, but the working path runs through the third-party dependency under review. Removing that dependency removes the capability.
surface_state_meanings.SHIPPED_OWNED_INPROCESS: Owned code exists and is reachable, but it stops at the process boundary; there is no production path to the external consumer.
surface_state_meanings.TEST_ONLY: The code exists but is gated to test or fuzz builds, so it is not a production capability and may not be cited as one.
surface_state_meanings.NOT_SHIPPED: Does not exist today. Recorded so an ADR cannot silently imply that it does.

adrs.title: Preserve arbitrary downstream Protobuf messages and ergonomic authoring
adrs.decision_summary: `prost` stays as the public authoring and codec boundary. `ProstCodec<T, U>` is an unrestricted generic surface: the struct carries no bounds at all, and the `Codec` impl accepts any `T: prost::Message + Send + 'static` and `U: prost::Message + Default + Send + 'static`, so any downstream crate can plug in its own derived or generated message type. The claim-time source read produced the argument that settles this. The finite message sets that the Rev-3 plan proposed to hand-write in exchange for dropping prost — gRPC health and reflection — are ALREADY prost-free today, and the only closed prost message set in the crate, `otlp_logs_proto`, is module-private. So prost buys exactly one thing: the arbitrary downstream generic surface. Trading it for a finite set would surrender the entire capability while gaining nothing that is not already owned. Owning further finite internal message sets is permitted and already happens; it is not a path to removing prost.

alternatives_considered.option: Replace `ProstCodec` with an owned `ProtoMessage` trait over a finite hand-written message set, per the Rev-3 plan.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: It would delete `ProstCodec<T, U>`, `SymmetricProstCodec<T>`, and both prost-typed `ProtobufError` variants, and would break the executable downstream journey in tests/fixtures/dependency-capability-baseline-consumer plus six conformance tests and eight fuzz targets. The bead states outright that a finite hand-written set removes functionality and is forbidden, and the capability registry's no-claim boundary says finite in-repo schemas cannot replace arbitrary downstream Protobuf capability.

alternatives_considered.option: Justify the finite set by pointing at gRPC health, reflection, and status-details as the messages that matter.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: Those surfaces contain zero prost references today. src/grpc/health.rs and src/grpc/reflection.rs are already hand-written and prost-free, so this alternative describes work that is already done and would not remove the dependency. It mistakes the internal message sets for the capability.

alternatives_considered.option: Own a `ProtoMessage` trait plus a production-quality derive macro and codegen, matching prost's ergonomics.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: Not rejected in principle, but it is a very large piece of work that must clear a high bar before it can be evaluated: arbitrary downstream compile and runtime fixtures, cross-language Protobuf and gRPC interop, malformed and resource-limit behavior, fuzzing, and rollback. Manual trait implementation alone is explicitly not equivalent ergonomics. Until that exists and passes, KEEP.

alternatives_considered.option: Narrow the public surface to `SymmetricProstCodec<T>` only, since it is the common case.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: Asymmetric request and response types are the normal gRPC shape, and the doc example itself uses `ProstCodec<HelloRequest, HelloResponse>`. Collapsing the two parameters is generic-API narrowing.

alternatives_considered.option: Make `prost` optional behind a feature so it leaves the default graph.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: `prost = "0.14"` is currently a plain non-optional dependency, so protobuf support is unconditional on native targets. Gating it would remove capability from every consumer who does not opt in, which is narrowing by another name. If the marginal graph cost is the concern, that is a measurement question for the marginal ledger, not a licence to gate a shipped public API.

preserved_public_symbols.note: The blessed short path. `pub mod grpc` is platform-gated to non-wasm32 but carries no feature gate, so this is default-feature public API.

`SymmetricProstCodec<T>` is NOT re-exported at `asupersync::grpc` and is reachable only by this long path; it is public API regardless. `ProstCodec::new`, `Default`, and `Clone` are all implemented without bounds, so a codec value can be constructed for any pair of types.
The generic seam `ProstCodec` implements. Client and server are generic over `Codec`, which is what makes a downstream `ProstCodec<Req, Resp>` usable end to end.
`GrpcClient<C>` is generic over `Codec`, defaulting to `IdentityCodec`.
Server-side `framed_codec` is generic over `Codec` on the same seam.
Streaming must keep working with the generic codec, not only with unary calls; the bead requires generic codec use in both.
Service description surface downstream authors implement alongside their own messages.
Status mapping is part of the interop contract; codec errors surface through it.
Already hand-written and prost-free. Frozen here as evidence that the finite internal message sets do not require prost, which is the core of this ADR's argument.
Also already prost-free.

preserved_feature_flags.name: default
preserved_feature_flags.effect: The protobuf surface is NOT behind any feature. `prost` is a plain non-optional dependency, so `ProstCodec` and the gRPC stack are available in a default build on non-wasm32 targets. This row exists to pin that fact: making protobuf feature-gated would be capability narrowing.
preserved_feature_flags.no_tokio_guarantee: prost's only dependencies are bytes and prost-derive; it introduces no tokio edge.

preserved_feature_flags.name: compression
preserved_feature_flags.effect: Gates the gzip frame compressor and decompressor used with `FramedCodec` around `ProstCodec`, and the gzip parity conformance coverage.

preserved_feature_flags.name: fuzz
preserved_feature_flags.effect: Enables the arbitrary-derive support used by the eight `ProstCodec` fuzz targets, and separately the quarantined OTLP proto helpers.
preserved_feature_flags.no_tokio_guarantee: Explicitly excluded from the no-Tokio production guarantee via the opentelemetry-proto edge; that carve-out is documented by DEP-ADR-003.

preserved_surfaces.note: The whole capability. Unrestricted in the type parameters; the size limit is enforced before encode via encoded_len and before decode, so oversized messages are rejected without allocating.
Already owned and prost-free. Any owned protobuf implementation would plug in here rather than replacing this.
Decisive for this ADR: the finite sets the Rev-3 plan wanted to hand-write in exchange for dropping prost already exist without it.

preserved_surfaces.wire_encoder: hand-rolled prost derives in a module-private message set
preserved_surfaces.note: The only closed prost message set in the crate. It is module-private and does not exercise the generic codec, so it is not evidence about the generic capability. Owned by DEP-ADR-003.

There is no src/codec/proto.rs and no owned ProtoMessage trait. The varint helpers in src/grpc/protobuf.rs are cfg(test) differential-oracle code, not reusable production code, and must not be cited as a partial implementation.

Neither prost-build nor prost-types is a dependency and there is no build-script codegen. Downstream authors rely on prost's derive macro, which is exactly the ergonomics an owned replacement would have to reproduce.

preserved_wire_contract.encoding: Protocol Buffers as implemented by prost 0.14
preserved_wire_contract.signal_paths_note: Length-prefixed message framing is one compression byte followed by a big-endian u32 length, then the encoded message. Byte parity with other gRPC implementations is an explicit conformance claim in the repository's own test suite.
preserved_wire_contract.http_status_semantics: gRPC status codes via the owned Code and Status types
preserved_wire_contract.collector_interop: Cross-language Protobuf and gRPC interoperability with other implementations is part of the capability, not an optional extra.
preserved_wire_contract.accepted_data_model: All Protobuf scalar and wire types, packed fields, maps, oneofs, repeated and nested messages, enums, and unknown-field preservation, as accepted by prost 0.14. The downstream fixture exercises uint64, repeated string, a string-to-int64 map, and a two-variant oneof.

preserved_config_semantics.name: max_message_size
preserved_config_semantics.contract: Defaults to DEFAULT_MAX_MESSAGE_SIZE, 4 MiB. Enforced before encoding using the computed encoded length and before decoding, so an oversized message is rejected without allocating it.

preserved_config_semantics.name: size_error_reporting
preserved_config_semantics.contract: Carries both the actual size and the configured limit. Reducing this to an opaque error is a diagnostic regression.

preserved_config_semantics.name: error_variant_distinctness
preserved_config_semantics.contract: Encode failure, decode failure, and size-limit failure stay three distinct variants. The encode and decode variants currently wrap prost's own error types, which is itself part of the frozen surface.

preserved_config_semantics.name: varint_strictness
preserved_config_semantics.contract: A ten-byte varint encoding u64::MAX is accepted; a ten-byte varint with bits above u64, an eleven-byte varint, and an unterminated ten-byte varint are all rejected. The size limit is checked before decoding begins.

preserved_config_semantics.name: unknown_field_policy
preserved_config_semantics.contract: Whatever prost 0.14 does for unknown fields is the accepted behavior, and schema evolution depends on it. Any owned replacement must match it exactly, not approximately.

preserved_config_semantics.name: streaming_use
preserved_config_semantics.surface: FramedCodec around ProstCodec in client and server streaming
preserved_config_semantics.contract: Message ordering is preserved across long streams; the repository pins a hundred-message server-streaming ordering case.

preserved_config_semantics.name: compression_interop
preserved_config_semantics.contract: gzip and identity frames must decode to an identical message tree, with no double decoding.

known_gaps.summary: The capability registry records source_owners for CAP-PROTOBUF-GENERIC as src/grpc/mod.rs and src/encoding.rs. src/encoding.rs is the RaptorQ FEC encoding pipeline and contains zero occurrences of prost or protobuf, and src/grpc/protobuf.rs, which actually defines ProstCodec and ProtobufError, is not named at all.
known_gaps.consequence: Inventory or baseline work that trusts that row will read an unrelated FEC module and miss the file that owns the capability. This is the second confirmed instance of the same defect class in the registry.

known_gaps.summary: Two files under src/ exercise ProstCodec with downstream-style messages over real HTTP/2 gRPC streaming, but neither is declared as a module anywhere, so neither is ever compiled.
known_gaps.consequence: They look like the richest end-to-end downstream-message journeys in the tree but provide zero coverage. They may not be counted as evidence while they remain undeclared.

known_gaps.summary: There is no gRPC or protobuf example under examples/, and the module-level doc example showing a downstream author defining messages and building a ProstCodec is inside an ignore fence, so it is never compiled.
known_gaps.consequence: The primary authoring journey this ADR protects has no executed demonstration outside the standalone consumer fixture.

known_gaps.summary: ProtobufError wraps prost's own encode and decode error types in two of its three variants, so the public error surface is not prost-free.
known_gaps.consequence: Any replacement changes the public error type, not merely the internal codec. That cost belongs in the replacement's parity budget and must not be discovered late.

known_gaps.summary: ProstCodec does not override the Codec trait's set_max_encode_message_size or set_max_decode_message_size, whose default bodies are no-ops, so runtime limit renegotiation never reaches it. Only construction-time with_max_size has effect.
known_gaps.consequence: An operator or peer-negotiated message-size change does not apply to a ProstCodec. This is current behavior and is frozen as such, but it is a real limitation rather than a designed guarantee.

known_gaps.summary: The capability baseline records CAP-PROTOBUF-GENERIC as EXECUTABLE_PARTIAL_BLOCKING: the positive, empty and boundary, malformed and error, and resource-limit cases have evidence, but cancellation cleanup is blocked on an owner and recovery is blocked externally.
known_gaps.consequence: Cancellation and recovery behavior for the generic codec is unproven, so a cutover cannot claim lifecycle parity today.

security_invariants: Untrusted wire input stays bounded: the size limit is enforced before decode, and malformed varints, wire types, lengths, depths, and truncation are rejected rather than absorbed.
The decode path allocates only after the size check passes, so an oversized declared length cannot drive allocation.
The unknown-field policy is explicit and inherited from prost; it may not silently change under a replacement.
The codec kernel stays strictly safe: no unsafe code is introduced on the protobuf path.
cancellation_invariants: Partial frames remain owned by the connection and are not leaked on cancellation.
Stream cancellation releases buffers and any reservations held by the framed codec.
These are stated obligations, not proven ones; PB-GAP-06 records that the cancellation and recovery cases are currently blocked.

platform_cells.note: The registry scopes CAP-PROTOBUF-GENERIC to all supported platforms and to the default feature set.
`pub mod grpc` is gated to non-wasm32, so the protobuf and gRPC surface is absent on wasm32 by construction. That exclusion is pre-existing and is not a loss introduced here.

entry_points: asupersync::grpc::ProstCodec as a codec over any downstream prost::Message
prost's own derive macro, used by downstream crates to author message types
external_ecosystem_integration.accepted_providers: Any type implementing prost::Message, whether hand-derived downstream or produced by prost-build in the consumer's own build script.
external_ecosystem_integration.no_reexport_note: asupersync does not re-export prost, so downstream consumers depend on it directly and must resolve to a compatible version. The standalone consumer fixture pins prost to exactly 0.14.4 and asserts that pin, which makes a prost major bump a downstream-visible break requiring its own evidence.
external_ecosystem_integration.runtime_seam_is_clean: The Codec trait, the framing layer, and the client and server seams are all owned and prost-free. The dependency is confined to the message type bound and the two wrapped error variants.
external_ecosystem_integration.removal_precondition: An owned replacement must provide an authoring experience at least as usable as prost's derive, accept arbitrary downstream schemas, match the full accepted data model including maps, oneofs, packed fields and unknown-field evolution, preserve the error surface or justify changing it, and pass arbitrary-downstream compile and runtime fixtures, cross-language Protobuf and gRPC interop, malformed and resource tests, fuzzing, and rollback. Manual trait implementation alone does not qualify as equivalent ergonomics unless the owner explicitly finds it better after consumer trials. Until then: KEEP.

user_journeys.description: Downstream author derives their own prost message with scalars, repeated fields, a map, and a oneof, builds a ProstCodec over it, and round-trips it. This is executed today by the standalone consumer fixture, which deliberately builds without test-internals.
Author uses distinct request and response types through ProstCodec<Req, Resp> in a unary gRPC call, the shape the module documentation itself demonstrates.
Author uses the generic codec for client, server, and bidirectional streaming, relying on preserved message ordering across long streams.
Operator sets a message size limit and receives a MessageTooLarge error naming both the actual size and the limit, rather than an opaque failure.
Messages encoded by asupersync are consumed by a non-Rust gRPC implementation and vice versa, relying on exact wire-byte compatibility.
Author enables gzip framing and gets an identical decoded message tree to the identity path.

api_surface_delta.rationale: This ADR makes no source change. Every frozen symbol lives under `asupersync::grpc`, not at the crate root, and the capability registry pins the api surface map by semantic hash.

supersedes.stale_text: owned ProtoMessage trait over a finite message set; drop the public arbitrary-prost::Message surface
supersedes.resolution: Rejected by the no-loss gate. Dropping the arbitrary surface is precisely the functionality removal this ADR exists to prevent.

supersedes.stale_text: Owned ProtoMessage trait plus hand-written finite message set (gRPC health/reflection/status-details; OTLP export subset) replaces prost
supersedes.resolution: The premise does not hold. The gRPC health and reflection message sets are already hand-written and prost-free, and the OTLP subset is a module-private set owned by DEP-ADR-003. Building those does not remove prost, because prost is required only for the arbitrary downstream generic surface.

supersedes.stale_text: OWN (SAFE) ... owned ProtoMessage trait + finite hand-written message types replace the public generic ProstCodec
supersedes.resolution: Disposition is KEEP_UNTIL_PARITY, not OWN. The row's dependent claim that the OpenTelemetry replacement depends on the prost replacement is also unnecessary: an owned OTLP message set can be written with prost derives exactly as otlp_logs_proto already is.

migration_policy.additive_only: Owning further finite internal message sets is permitted and already happens. Doing so adds capability; it does not subtract the generic surface and is not a step toward removing prost.
migration_policy.coexistence: prost remains the public authoring and codec boundary. An owned protobuf implementation, if ever built, would plug into the existing Codec seam alongside ProstCodec rather than replacing it, until parity is proven.
migration_policy.sequencing: The baseline corpus for the full accepted data model must exist before any replacement is evaluable, and the currently blocked cancellation and recovery cases must be unblocked before lifecycle parity can be claimed.
migration_policy.docs_obligation: Any change to the frozen surface updates this artifact, docs/dependency_api_adr_registry.md, and docs/adr/dep_plan_adr_002_protobuf_generic.md in the same commit.

rollback_policy.trigger: Any downstream crate that can no longer author or use its own message type, any narrowing of the accepted data model, any loss of a ProtobufError variant or of the size and limit detail, any wire-byte divergence from other gRPC implementations, any streaming ordering change, or any prost major bump that breaks the pinned consumer fixture.
rollback_policy.action: Revert to the frozen surface recorded here. Because the decision is KEEP, rollback means abandoning the replacement attempt rather than restoring a deleted capability.
rollback_policy.verification: Re-run the focused ADR contract, the six gRPC codec conformance tests, the eight ProstCodec fuzz targets, and the standalone downstream consumer fixture before declaring the rollback complete.

required_evidence_classes: unit: full accepted data model including scalars, repeated, packed, maps, enums, oneofs, nested messages, and unknown-field evolution
unit: empty message, boundary and maximum sizes, malformed varints, wrong wire types, truncation, and recursion depth
unit: cancellation, race, shutdown, leak, and quiescence behavior for the framed codec, which PB-GAP-06 records as currently blocked
property: round-trip idempotence over generated message trees
differential: byte-for-byte agreement with prost for encode and decode, and length-prefixed framing parity with other gRPC implementations
fuzz: the existing ProstCodec fuzz targets covering decode, huge messages, framing, and malformed varint overflow
downstream-consumer: a standalone crate outside the workspace authoring its own message with map and oneof fields, compiled without test-internals, with its prost version pinned
cross-language E2E: interoperability with a non-Rust gRPC implementation in both directions
streaming E2E: ordering preserved across long client, server, and bidirectional streams
evidence.note: Naming these owners does not assert they have run. The two undeclared files recorded in PB-GAP-02 and the ignore-fenced doc example in PB-GAP-03 may not be counted toward any of these classes.

cutover.note: This ADR authorizes no dependency exit. prost remains a non-optional production dependency. Phase-5 protobuf children inherit the KEEP and must not proceed on the assumption that the generic surface is being retired.

adrs.no_claim_boundary: This ADR is a frozen decision and public-surface inventory only. It does not prove that the planned evidence has run, that cross-language interoperability has been demonstrated, that cancellation and recovery behavior is correct, that an owned protobuf implementation could reach ergonomic or wire parity, that performance is unchanged, or that prost may be removed. It also does not certify the capability registry's source-owner rows, which PB-GAP-01 records as incorrect for this capability.

adrs.title: Preserve OTLP metrics + traces + logs and external SDK/provider/collector interoperability
adrs.decision_summary: Keep both telemetry tiers that ship today, because they are not redundant: they cover different signals. Tier 1 is the owned, hand-rolled OTLP surface, which reaches the wire in production for the logs signal only. Tier 2 is the external OpenTelemetry ecosystem bridge, and for the metrics and traces signals it is the only production export path that exists. The three `OtelMetrics` constructors each take an `opentelemetry::metrics::Meter` supplied by the embedder, and the re-exported `SpanStorage` type materializes spans through an embedder-supplied `opentelemetry::trace::BoxedTracer`. Deleting the `opentelemetry` and `opentelemetry_sdk` dependencies would therefore not merely remove an optional integration; it would leave asupersync with no production metrics or traces export at all. The dependencies are KEEP_UNTIL_PARITY and the capability stays KEEP_INCUMBENT.

alternatives_considered.option: Remove `opentelemetry` and `opentelemetry_sdk`; ship only the owned OTLP/HTTP exporters.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: The owned OTLP request builders for the metrics and traces signals live in `observability::otel::otlp_request_builder`, which is gated `#[cfg(all(any(test, feature = "fuzz"), feature = "metrics", feature = "tracing-integration"))]`. They are unreachable in any production build. Removing the ecosystem crates would delete the only production metrics and traces export path and also delete `OtelMetrics::new`, the sole integration point for downstream code that already owns a `MeterProvider`. That is compound capability loss.

alternatives_considered.option: Keep the OTLP wire path for two of the three signals and drop the third.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: `otlp-logs-omission` is a named historical loss fixture in the capability registry. The logs signal is in fact the single best-supported one: `LogsSnapshot::to_otlp_protobuf` and the `otlp_logs_proto` prost message set are ungated inside the `metrics`-gated module, so they encode and send in production today. Dropping it would remove the only owned end-to-end OTLP wire path in the crate.

alternatives_considered.option: Route the owned trace pipeline through the ecosystem crates and delete `otlp_trace_exporter`.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: `observability::otlp_trace_exporter` is ungated: its types, bounded queue, head-based sampling, and brownout policy are available at default features with no `opentelemetry` dependency. Folding it into the ecosystem crates would make that surface feature-gated and would add a dependency edge to the default production graph.

alternatives_considered.option: Promote `otlp_request_builder` out of its test/fuzz gate so metrics and traces get an owned production wire path.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: It depends on `opentelemetry-proto`, which is deliberately quarantined behind `fuzz` because its `gen-tonic-messages` feature pulls `tonic` and therefore `tokio`. Promoting it as written would put a tokio edge in the metrics production graph and break the no-Tokio guarantee. Closing this gap requires an owned prost message set in the style of `otlp_logs_proto`, which is real implementation work owned by asupersync-5z2scg.2, not an ADR decision.

alternatives_considered.option: Enable the `logs` feature on the `opentelemetry`/`opentelemetry_sdk` crates to back the logs signal.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: The production `metrics` feature deliberately pins both crates to `default-features = false, features = ["metrics", "trace"]`. Widening that set grows the production graph for a signal that already has a working owned implementation. Deferred, not rejected on principle.

preserved_public_symbols.note: Dependency-free in-process metrics registry and the runtime's `MetricsProvider` seam. Available with no Cargo features enabled and entirely free of OpenTelemetry types.
Owned in-process OTLP trace pipeline. Ungated: available at default features with no `opentelemetry` dependency.

Ungated re-export, but `SpanStorage` methods take and return `opentelemetry::Context`, `BoxedTracer`, `BoxedSpan`, `Status`, and `Value`. This is a hard ecosystem coupling on a type reachable at default features.
W3C Trace Context and Baggage propagation, implemented without any OpenTelemetry crate dependency.
Curated `metrics`-gated re-export set from `observability::otel`.

`pub mod otel` is public, so every `pub` item is reachable API even when it is absent from the curated re-export list. `OtlpHttpExporter` and `PrivacyConfig` in particular are reachable only by the long path, and `PrivacyConfig` already has an external-consumer smoke fixture under tests/fixtures/dependency-capability-baseline-consumer.

preserved_feature_flags.name: metrics
preserved_feature_flags.effect: Enables `observability::otel` (owned OTLP/HTTP logs exporter, the shared `OtlpHttpExporter` transport, the external `Meter` bridge, privacy/redaction, and cardinality control) plus `observability::histogram_conformance`. `regex` is required by the PII redaction engine.
preserved_feature_flags.no_tokio_guarantee: The `metrics` production graph must have no normal-edge dependency on tokio. Proof lane `metrics-production-tokio-tree`: `cargo tree -e normal -p asupersync --features metrics -i tokio` must print `warning: nothing to print.`

preserved_feature_flags.name: tracing-integration
preserved_feature_flags.effect: Enables the real `observability::otel::span_semantics` module; without it a stub is compiled instead. Also required, together with `test`/`fuzz`, to reach `otlp_request_builder`.
preserved_feature_flags.no_tokio_guarantee: Not an OTLP transport dependency; listed because the capability registry maps it to CAP-OTLP-ECOSYSTEM.

preserved_feature_flags.name: compression
preserved_feature_flags.effect: Enables gzip request-body compression in `OtlpHttpExporter`. Without it, calling `with_compression(true)` is a hard error rather than a silent downgrade.

preserved_feature_flags.name: fuzz
preserved_feature_flags.effect: Enables `opentelemetry-proto` with `gen-tonic-messages`, `trace`, `metrics`, and `logs`, which is what makes `otlp_request_builder` reachable for conformance, golden, and fuzz helpers.
preserved_feature_flags.no_tokio_guarantee: Explicitly EXCLUDED from the no-Tokio production guarantee. Proof lane `fuzz-tokio-quarantine-tree` expects the `opentelemetry-proto` -> `tonic`/`tonic-prost` -> `tokio` path and treats it as an accepted, documented quarantine edge.

preserved_surfaces.wire_encoder: LogsSnapshot::to_otlp_protobuf via the ungated internal `otlp_logs_proto` prost message set
preserved_surfaces.note: The only signal with a complete owned production path from snapshot to wire. Implemented WITHOUT the ecosystem crates' logs feature. `otlp-logs-omission` is a named historical loss fixture; this signal may not be dropped.

preserved_surfaces.wire_encoder: none in production; `otlp_request_builder::metrics_request_from_snapshot` is gated to test/fuzz
preserved_surfaces.transport: the embedder's own opentelemetry_sdk reader and exporter
preserved_surfaces.note: `OtelMetrics` records into real `opentelemetry` instruments obtained from a caller-supplied `Meter`. Production metrics therefore leave the process through the embedder's SDK pipeline, not through asupersync. The dependency-free `observability::metrics` registry and its Prometheus exposition text format remain available at default features as a separate, non-OTLP path.

preserved_surfaces.wire_encoder: none in production; `otlp_request_builder::traces_request` is gated to test/fuzz
preserved_surfaces.transport: the embedder's own opentelemetry_sdk tracer for exported spans; the owned pipeline is in-process only
preserved_surfaces.note: The owned trace pipeline ships ungated with bounded queues, head-based sampling, and brownout policy, but the only shipped `TraceExporter` implementation buffers in memory. Spans that actually reach a collector do so through the embedder's SDK via `SpanStorage` and `BoxedTracer`. Tail-based sampling is explicitly and deliberately unsupported, pinned by `otlp_tail_based_sampling_scope`.

`OtelMetrics::new(Meter)`, `OtelMetrics::new_with_resource_detection(Meter, ...)`, and `OtelMetrics::new_with_config(Meter, MetricsConfig)` all accept a `Meter` from ANY downstream `MeterProvider`. This is the whole third-party-ecosystem interop capability and the primary reason the `opentelemetry` dependency is KEEP_UNTIL_PARITY.

preserved_wire_contract.signal_paths_note: The endpoint is caller-supplied verbatim. Asupersync does not append `/v1/logs`, `/v1/metrics`, or `/v1/traces`, and must not begin silently rewriting caller paths.
preserved_wire_contract.temporality: Cumulative only. Hardcoded in the request builders and guarded by a source-text regression test that fails if a Delta path appears without prev-value and reset tracking.
preserved_wire_contract.http_status_semantics: 2xx OK; 408, 429, and 502-504 retryable honoring Retry-After; 405 non-retryable echoing the Allow header; 415 triggers a single uncompressed retry; all other 4xx and 5xx are non-retryable with the batch dropped.
preserved_wire_contract.retry_jitter: Deterministic, not random, so replay stays reproducible.
preserved_wire_contract.collector_interop: Content type, resource and scope attributes, severity mapping, partial-success handling, throttling, and Retry-After parsing must stay collector-compatible.

preserved_config_semantics.name: endpoint
preserved_config_semantics.contract: Caller-supplied full signal URL, used verbatim.

preserved_config_semantics.name: timeout
preserved_config_semantics.contract: Per-attempt timeout, default 10s. Expiry maps to a non-retryable error and the batch is dropped rather than requeued, which is what keeps exporter memory bounded.

preserved_config_semantics.name: retry
preserved_config_semantics.contract: max_retries default 3, initial delay default 100ms, max delay default 30s, exponential doubling clamped to max delay, Retry-After taking precedence when present. There is no retry queue; a single body is held across attempts.

preserved_config_semantics.name: compression
preserved_config_semantics.contract: gzip request bodies, default OFF. The default must not silently change. Requesting compression without the `compression` feature is a hard error, never a silent downgrade.

preserved_config_semantics.name: auth
preserved_config_semantics.contract: Headers are attached to every request. They must be treated as secret material by any redaction, logging, or diagnostics surface.

preserved_config_semantics.name: tls
preserved_config_semantics.contract: Fail-closed. With neither `tls-native-roots` nor `tls-webpki-roots`, the root store is empty and the client build fails. There is no silent system-CA fallback and no HTTPS-to-HTTP downgrade; TLS errors are non-retryable.

preserved_config_semantics.name: resource_attributes
preserved_config_semantics.contract: Three sources with fixed precedence: built-in defaults, then `OTEL_RESOURCE_ATTRIBUTES`, then programmatic attributes. Host-name detection is opt-in.

preserved_config_semantics.name: scope_attributes
preserved_config_semantics.contract: Defaults are the pinned scope name and schema URL; both are overridable per snapshot.

preserved_config_semantics.name: cardinality
preserved_config_semantics.contract: Bounded unique label combinations per metric and bounded distinct metric names, with an explicit overflow strategy of Drop, Aggregate, or Warn and an observable overflow count.

preserved_config_semantics.name: privacy_redaction
preserved_config_semantics.contract: Attribute and label drop lists, a glob allowlist, custom regex patterns, and built-in detectors for email, SSN, Luhn-validated payment cards, and phone numbers. Applies across traces, metrics, and logs. Redaction may only widen, never narrow.

preserved_config_semantics.name: attribute_caps
preserved_config_semantics.contract: 128 attributes and 4096 value bytes, with `dropped_attributes_count` accounting rather than silent truncation.

preserved_config_semantics.name: sampling
preserved_config_semantics.contract: Per-metric sample rates plus a head-based span filter that drops unsampled spans before export. Sampling decisions are deterministic.

preserved_config_semantics.name: load_shedding
preserved_config_semantics.contract: Bounded queues shed with counted drops. The metrics queue drops newest; the trace queue drops oldest to preserve recency. Trace shedding is driven by runtime resource-monitor brownout levels with three actions: export all, drop low priority, retain summary only.

known_gaps.summary: No owned production wire encoder for the metrics and traces signals. `otlp_request_builder` is gated to test and fuzz builds because it depends on the tokio-carrying `opentelemetry-proto`.
known_gaps.consequence: Production metrics and traces export depends entirely on the embedder's OpenTelemetry SDK. This is the strongest single argument against removing the ecosystem crates.

known_gaps.summary: The synchronous `MetricsExporter::export` and `LogsExporter::export` implementations on the HTTP exporters return an error directing callers to the async path, because the real send requires an explicit `&Cx`.
known_gaps.consequence: HTTP exporters cannot be driven through the exporter trait objects; callers must hold the concrete type and an async context.

known_gaps.summary: `OtelMetrics::new_with_resource_detection` builds the resource attribute set and then discards it, on the documented assumption that the caller's `Meter` already carries those attributes.
known_gaps.consequence: Resource detection is advisory at that entry point rather than effective.

known_gaps.summary: Only `OTEL_RESOURCE_ATTRIBUTES` is honored. There is no support for the `OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_*` environment configuration family, and no periodic reader or collection-interval scheduling.
known_gaps.consequence: Operators configure the exporter programmatically; export cadence is entirely the embedder's responsibility.

known_gaps.summary: The owned log body encoder supports only the string variant of the OTLP AnyValue union.
known_gaps.consequence: Integer, double, boolean, array, and key-value-list log bodies are not representable on the owned wire path.

known_gaps.summary: Roughly 39 OTLP audit test files under src/observability are tracked but not declared in mod.rs, so they never compile. This quarantine is deliberate and documented in artifacts/otlp_audit_cluster_inventory_v1.json under the rule that blocked preserved files must not be listed until they compile against real production seams.
known_gaps.consequence: A large body of OTLP failure-mode coverage is inert and must not be counted as evidence.

known_gaps.summary: Tail-based sampling is explicitly unsupported, pinned by an explicit support-class contract rather than silently missing.
known_gaps.consequence: Not a defect. Recorded so that the explicit unsupported declaration is not mistaken for an accidental omission.

security_invariants: TLS configuration is fail-closed: an empty root store fails the client build rather than falling back to system CAs, and TLS errors never downgrade HTTPS to HTTP.
Bearer tokens, API keys, and custom auth headers are secret material and must not reach logs, traces, diagnostics, or error text.
The shared redaction policy applies to metrics, traces, and logs alike; no signal may bypass it.
The `metrics` production graph keeps its no-normal-edge-on-tokio guarantee; `opentelemetry-proto` stays quarantined behind `fuzz`.
Attribute count and value-size caps bound untrusted attribute input, with counted drops rather than silent truncation.
cancellation_invariants: Exporter work takes an explicit `&Cx` and is owned by the caller's region; export tasks may not outlive the region that created them.
Flush is bounded, and the trace exporter's Drop-path flush is bounded by an explicit shutdown timeout and skipped entirely when the queue is empty, so shutdown cannot deadlock.
A timed-out or cancelled export drops its batch with a counted outcome rather than orphaning it or leaving a retry loop running.
Bounded export queues shed load with observable counts rather than blocking a runtime worker.

platform_cells.note: Full OTLP/HTTP export path over the crate's own HTTP/1.1 client.
The capability registry scopes CAP-OTLP-ECOSYSTEM to `native`. Browser telemetry is a separate Browser Edition surface and is out of scope for this ADR.

external_ecosystem_integration.accepted_providers: Any implementation of `opentelemetry::metrics::MeterProvider`, including `opentelemetry_sdk::metrics::SdkMeterProvider` and third-party providers such as Prometheus bridges.
external_ecosystem_integration.no_reexport_note: There is no `pub use opentelemetry` anywhere in the crate. Coupling is by function signature, so downstream consumers must pin a compatible `opentelemetry` version themselves. Any change to the pinned major version is a downstream-visible break and requires downstream-consumer evidence.
external_ecosystem_integration.instrument_surface: Counters, histograms, and observable gauges covering task, region, cancellation, budget, deadline, obligation, and scheduler instrumentation, exposed through the OpenTelemetry-free `MetricsProvider` trait at the runtime seam.
external_ecosystem_integration.runtime_seam_is_clean: `RuntimeBuilder::metrics` is generic over asupersync's own `MetricsProvider` trait and leaks no OpenTelemetry types.
external_ecosystem_integration.removal_precondition: An owned adapter must accept the same downstream provider handles and reproduce every instrument, attribute, temporality, and aggregation behavior, AND an owned tokio-free production wire encoder must exist for the metrics and traces signals, both proved by real-collector and reference-SDK evidence. Until then: KEEP.

user_journeys.description: Operator enables the `metrics` feature, builds an `OtlpLogsHttpExporter` against a collector endpoint, and ships logs over OTLP/HTTP protobuf with no OpenTelemetry SDK in their own code.
Consumer uses `TraceExporter`, `OtlpSpan`, and `SpanBatch` at DEFAULT features, with no `metrics` feature, for in-process span batching, sampling, and brownout shedding.

Consumer already owns an `SdkMeterProvider` or a third-party provider, takes a `Meter` from it, and passes it to `OtelMetrics::new` so asupersync runtime instrumentation lands in their existing pipeline. This is the only production metrics export journey.
Consumer uses the dependency-free `observability::metrics` registry and its Prometheus exposition text format with no OTLP and no OpenTelemetry crates at all.

Operator runs against a misbehaving collector and gets distinct, actionable outcomes for throttling, partial success, auth failure, TLS failure, timeout, unsupported method, and compression rejection rather than one opaque error.
Application cancels its region during export and reaches quiescence within its budget with counted drops and no orphaned batches or retry loops.

api_surface_delta.rationale: This ADR makes no source change. `artifacts/api_surface_map_v1.json` tracks crate-root exports from src/lib.rs only, and every symbol frozen here lives under `asupersync::observability`, not the crate root. The capability registry additionally pins that map by semantic hash, so editing it here would be both unnecessary and destructive.

supersedes.stale_text: explicit decision to remove external OpenTelemetry Meter/SDK interoperability (or abandon the replacement)
supersedes.resolution: Both branches are rejected by the Rev-5 no-loss gate. The terminal decision is additive coexistence with KEEP_UNTIL_PARITY.

supersedes.stale_text: 0 external if ADR 3.3 approves dropping external-SDK interop
supersedes.resolution: ADR 3.3 does not approve it. The projected zero-external-dependency metrics graph is not an authorized outcome.

migration_policy.additive_only: New owned surfaces are added alongside existing ones. No accepted entry point is renamed away, deprecated behind an alias, or narrowed.
migration_policy.coexistence: The owned tier and the ecosystem bridge coexist indefinitely. Documentation may recommend the owned tier as the default path for logs without weakening the bridge, which remains the only production path for metrics and traces.
migration_policy.sequencing: Closing OTLP-GAP-01 with an owned tokio-free wire encoder is a precondition for even discussing a dependency exit, and is itself gated behind real-collector and reference-SDK parity evidence.
migration_policy.docs_obligation: Any change to the frozen surface updates this artifact, docs/dependency_api_adr_registry.md, and docs/adr/dep_plan_adr_003_otlp_ecosystem.md in the same commit.

rollback_policy.trigger: Any downstream consumer build break, collector interop failure, lost signal, silently changed default, new tokio normal-edge in the metrics graph, or narrowed redaction.
rollback_policy.action: Revert to the frozen surface recorded here. Because the decision is coexistence, rollback is a revert of an additive change rather than resurrection of a deleted capability.
rollback_policy.verification: Re-run the focused contract lane plus the CAP-OTLP-ECOSYSTEM scenario IDs and the two tokio proof lanes before declaring the rollback complete.

required_evidence_classes: unit: happy path, empty and maximum attribute counts and value sizes, malformed input, and distinct error mapping per failure class
unit: cancellation, race, shutdown, leak, and quiescence states for every exporter, including the bounded Drop-path flush
property and fuzz: OTLP wire-format encode and decode through the `fuzz` feature helpers
differential: owned logs encoder output compared against the reference proto encoding for identical input
sparse-feature: build and test matrix covering default, `metrics`, `metrics`+`tracing-integration`, and `metrics`+`compression`
downstream-consumer: a synthesized consumer owning an SdkMeterProvider that drives OtelMetrics::new, plus one using observability::otel::PrivacyConfig by long path

real-service E2E: a live collector accepting the logs signal on the owned path and the metrics and traces signals through a reference SDK, with partial-success, throttle, auth-failure, and TLS-failure rows
graph: both tokio proof lanes green, metrics clean and fuzz quarantined
evidence.note: Naming these owners does not assert they have run. BASELINE_PLANNED means the corpus is specified, not executed. The quarantined audit files recorded in OTLP-GAP-06 may not be counted toward any of these classes while they remain uncompiled.

cutover.note: This ADR authorizes no dependency exit. `opentelemetry` and `opentelemetry_sdk` remain production dependencies of the `metrics` feature.

adrs.no_claim_boundary: This ADR is a frozen decision and public-surface inventory only. It does not prove that the planned evidence has run, that the owned logs encoder is byte-compatible with any reference implementation, that a live collector accepts asupersync output, that metrics, traces, or logs parity has been measured, that performance is unchanged, that the workspace is healthy, or that any dependency may be removed. Agreement on the metrics signal alone, or on generated-message shapes alone, does not prove traces, logs, provider ecosystem, lifecycle, or real collector parity.

adrs.title: Additive canonical JSON while preserving accepted TOML config and YAML scenarios
adrs.decision_summary: TOML runtime/CLI configuration and YAML lab scenarios are operator- and author-facing accepted inputs and stay accepted. Canonical JSON is additive output and an additional accepted input; it never becomes the only accepted form. `toml` and `serde_yaml` remain KEEP_UNTIL_PARITY. Two facts from the claim-time source read shape this. First, the parsing surfaces are thinner than they look: the `Scenario` type contains no YAML code at all, only serde derives, and every YAML parse happens at a call site in a binary or a test, so `serde_yaml` never appears in a library public signature. Second, `serde_json` is already a non-optional dependency and `Scenario` already round-trips JSON, so scenario JSON is not a new capability. What genuinely does not exist is JSON configuration loading and any shared canonical-JSON encoder; both are recorded NOT_SHIPPED so this ADR cannot be read as implying they are present.

alternatives_considered.option: Migrate configuration and scenarios to canonical versioned JSON and stop accepting TOML and YAML.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: Both are accepted operator and author inputs with a live corpus: thirteen scenario YAML files across `examples/scenarios/`, `frankenlab/examples/scenarios/`, and `tools/demos/`, plus a documented `getting_started` journey that runs them. Dropping acceptance is direct user-journey loss and the no-loss gate rejects it.

alternatives_considered.option: Keep TOML and YAML, but make canonical JSON the primary on-disk format and demote the others to legacy.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: There is no canonical-JSON encoder in the crate to promote. `Scenario::to_json` uses `serde_json::to_string_pretty`, which is pretty-printed rather than byte-canonical, and the only canonicalization convention in the codebase is incidental `BTreeMap` key ordering plus insta snapshot goldens. Promoting a format that does not yet exist would freeze an aspiration.

alternatives_considered.option: Replace `serde_yaml` with an owned YAML parser now, since it is only used at three call sites.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: Call-site count understates the obligation. The accepted grammar is whatever `serde_yaml` 0.9 accepts across the live corpus — anchors, aliases, merge keys, tags, number and Unicode handling, and duplicate-key policy — and none of that is specified anywhere yet. `asupersync-5z2scg.5.1` owns establishing the accepted subset from evidence. Until that exists, an owned parser cannot be shown to preserve the capability.

alternatives_considered.option: Replace `toml` with the existing hand-rolled parser in `src/config.rs`, which already reads a TOML-shaped format.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: `src/config.rs` is not a TOML parser. It makes zero `toml::` calls and hand-splits lines on `=` with `[section]` headers, lowercasing section names and stripping `#` and `//` comments. It accepts a narrower, different grammar with different error semantics. Routing real TOML through it would silently narrow accepted input.

alternatives_considered.option: Add JSON configuration loading in this ADR.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: This bead is decision-only. The decision authorizes JSON config as additive, but the implementation, its precedence semantics, and its round-trip evidence belong to `asupersync-5z2scg.4` and its children.

preserved_public_symbols.note: The only place the `toml` crate parses runtime configuration. Both tables and every field are optional, so empty and partial documents are accepted; that tolerance is part of the contract.
Ungated, and part of the TOML contract because `parse_toml_file` takes an `&dyn EnvReader` and because these implement the precedence rule.
Public entry points on `RuntimeBuilder`, also reachable as `asupersync::runtime::RuntimeBuilder` and `asupersync::prelude::RuntimeBuilder`. Failures map to `ErrorKind::ConfigError`.
Operator-facing ATP configuration: layered scopes, source attribution, and an explain-resolution surface. TOML is both read and written here, so round-trip fidelity is a user-visible contract.

Ungated RaptorQ configuration with its own hand-rolled INI-style parser and an env prefix of RAPTORQ_. Frozen here because the capability registry names this file as a source owner, but see OTLP-unrelated gap CFG-GAP-01: it is not a `toml`-crate surface.

The scenario schema itself, ungated and free of any YAML dependency. Five of these types are NOT re-exported at `asupersync::lab` and are reachable only by the long `asupersync::lab::scenario::` path; both paths are frozen. `ValidationError` is re-exported under the renamed alias `ScenarioValidationError`.
Scenario execution, seed exploration, and replay validation. Also ungated and YAML-free.

preserved_feature_flags.name: config-file
preserved_feature_flags.effect: Enables `RuntimeBuilder::from_toml` / `from_toml_str` and the `runtime::env_config` TOML surface. Not in the default feature set.
preserved_feature_flags.no_tokio_guarantee: `toml` is a pure-Rust parser with no tokio edge.

preserved_feature_flags.name: dependency-ledger
preserved_feature_flags.effect: Reuses the same optional TOML parser for the marginal-ledger generator binary; deliberately does not enter production graphs.
preserved_feature_flags.no_tokio_guarantee: Same pure-Rust parser; internal tooling only.

preserved_feature_flags.name: cli
preserved_feature_flags.effect: The only feature that enables `serde_yaml`, and it also pulls in `config-file`. Frozen verbatim because the YAML scenario capability and the TOML config capability both depend on this composition.
preserved_feature_flags.no_tokio_guarantee: None of these edges introduce tokio.

preserved_surfaces.note: Accepts the twelve `[scheduler]` keys and the two `[blocking]` keys, all optional, with both tables defaulted. Field renaming happens on apply, not on parse.

preserved_surfaces.transport: layered config files across standard paths
preserved_surfaces.note: Serializes back out with `to_string_pretty`, so this is the surface where comment and formatting loss would actually be observed by an operator.

preserved_surfaces.wire_encoder: hand-rolled line parser, not the toml crate
preserved_surfaces.note: Already owned and dependency-free. It is NOT a TOML implementation and must not be treated as evidence that an owned TOML parser exists.

preserved_surfaces.wire_encoder: serde_yaml 0.9, invoked at call sites rather than inside the library types
preserved_surfaces.note: The accepted grammar is whatever serde_yaml 0.9 accepts over the live corpus; it has never been specified. `asupersync-5z2scg.5.1` owns pinning it. Include refs are security-validated: .yaml/.yml extension, length cap, restricted charset.
Scenario JSON already round-trips today, so JSON scenario support is not a new capability. `to_json` is pretty-printed, not byte-canonical.
Run, explore-seeds, and validate-replay are the behaviors any format change must keep bit-identical.
There is no `RuntimeBuilder::from_json`, no JSON path in env_config, and no JSON loading in the ATP or atpd config surfaces. This ADR authorizes adding it additively; it does not claim it exists.
No shared canonical-JSON type, trait, or helper exists. The de-facto convention is BTreeMap key ordering plus insta goldens. Whoever implements canonical JSON is introducing it, not adopting it.

preserved_wire_contract.protocol: local file formats, not a network protocol
preserved_wire_contract.encoding: TOML 1.0 for runtime and CLI configuration; YAML 1.2 as accepted by serde_yaml 0.9 for scenarios; JSON for scenario round-trip and, additively, for configuration
preserved_wire_contract.signal_paths_note: Config precedence is file (lowest), then environment, then programmatic (highest). That order is the contract and may not be reordered.
preserved_wire_contract.schema_versioning: Scenarios carry `schema_version`, defaulted via serde so older documents keep loading. `SCENARIO_SCHEMA_VERSION` is 1. Runtime TOML has no version field today; adding one must be backward-compatible.

preserved_config_semantics.name: precedence
preserved_config_semantics.surface: RuntimeBuilder::from_toml then with_env_overrides then programmatic setters
preserved_config_semantics.contract: File is lowest, environment overrides file, programmatic overrides both. Covered today by focused unit tests and must not be reordered or made format-dependent.

preserved_config_semantics.name: partial_and_empty_documents
preserved_config_semantics.contract: Both tables and all fields are optional. An empty document is valid and yields defaults. Making any field mandatory is accepted-input loss.

preserved_config_semantics.name: unknown_field_policy
preserved_config_semantics.contract: Current behavior is whatever serde derives produce without a deny-unknown-fields attribute. Tightening this is a narrowing change and requires its own evidence.

preserved_config_semantics.name: thread_name_prefix_validation
preserved_config_semantics.contract: Validated on apply with an actionable error rather than silently accepted.

preserved_config_semantics.name: config_error_diagnostics
preserved_config_semantics.contract: Syntax, type, unknown-field, precedence, path, and semantic validation failures stay distinguishable with actionable messages. Diagnostics may improve; they may not get coarser.

preserved_config_semantics.name: config_round_trip
preserved_config_semantics.contract: Configuration written back must remain loadable and semantically identical. Any comment or ordering loss is operator-visible and belongs in the migration evidence.

preserved_config_semantics.name: config_path_security
preserved_config_semantics.contract: The explicit secure variants exist and must keep their stricter path handling; the non-secure variants may not silently become the only option.

preserved_config_semantics.name: scenario_include_security
preserved_config_semantics.contract: Include paths require a .yaml or .yml extension, are length-capped, and use a restricted character set. This bound may only tighten in ways that keep the existing corpus valid.

preserved_config_semantics.name: scenario_validation
preserved_config_semantics.contract: Returns a list of located `ValidationError`s rather than failing on the first problem. Existing rejections (empty id, bad schema version, unordered faults, duplicate participants, missing cancellation count, unknown oracle) must keep failing for the same reason.

preserved_config_semantics.name: scenario_determinism
preserved_config_semantics.contract: Same scenario and seed produce the same fingerprint. A format change that perturbs field ordering, numeric parsing, or defaulting can break replay determinism and is therefore in scope for this ADR's evidence.

preserved_config_semantics.name: env_prefixes
preserved_config_semantics.contract: The runtime env override set and the RAPTORQ_ prefix are accepted operator inputs and stay accepted.

known_gaps.summary: The capability registry records `source_owners` for CAP-CONFIG-TOML-JSON as src/config.rs and src/bin/asupersync.rs. Neither makes a single `toml::` call. src/config.rs is a hand-rolled INI-style parser and src/bin/asupersync.rs has no TOML code at all. The real toml-crate owners are src/runtime/env_config.rs, src/runtime/builder.rs, src/cli/atp_config.rs, src/bin/atpd.rs, and src/bin/dependency_marginal_ledger.rs.
known_gaps.consequence: Any baseline or cutover work that trusts the registry's source_owners will inventory the wrong files and can miss the entire runtime and CLI TOML surface. The api_surface_map selector `config-reexports` has the same problem: it maps the prefix `config::` to this capability, which is the INI parser rather than the TOML surface.

known_gaps.summary: No integration test exercises `RuntimeBuilder::from_toml`, the file-path variant. Only `from_toml_str` is covered, by in-crate unit tests.
known_gaps.consequence: Path handling, IO error mapping, and file-not-found diagnostics for the primary documented entry point are untested.

known_gaps.summary: No cross-format equivalence test exists. `scenario_yaml_roundtrip` and `scenario_json_roundtrip` are independent single-format round-trips; nothing asserts that YAML and JSON produce the same Scenario.
known_gaps.consequence: The central claim of this ADR, that JSON is additive and lossless with respect to YAML, has no executable evidence yet. The registry already names `scenario_cross_format` as a planned scenario ID.

known_gaps.summary: The accepted YAML subset has never been specified. Anchor, alias, merge-key, tag, numeric, Unicode, and duplicate-key behavior are whatever serde_yaml 0.9 does over the corpus.
known_gaps.consequence: No owned parser can be shown to preserve the capability until the accepted subset is pinned from evidence.

known_gaps.summary: There is no checked-in example TOML configuration file and no doctested TOML journey. The two rustdoc examples on `from_toml` and `from_toml_str` are in ```ignore``` fences, and the documented path `config/runtime.toml` does not exist in the repo.
known_gaps.consequence: The operator-facing TOML journey is documented but never executed, so it can rot silently.

known_gaps.summary: `src/fs_config_metamorphic_tests.rs` provides TOML round-trip and canonical-form metamorphic coverage, but it operates on a local mock config struct rather than on `RuntimeTomlConfig`, and the module is gated behind `legacy-internal-test-harnesses`.
known_gaps.consequence: That coverage may not be cited as evidence for the real configuration types.

security_invariants: Secrets in configuration are redacted in diagnostics and never echoed into errors or logs.
Configuration cannot grant ambient file or network authority; unknown security-relevant fields fail closed.
The explicit secure read and write variants in the ATP config surface keep their stricter path handling.
Scenario include paths stay bounded by extension, length, and character-set validation, and untrusted scenario documents remain bounded in size, nesting, and collection count.
No scenario or configuration format may introduce implicit code execution.
cancellation_invariants: Configuration load is atomic with respect to the builder: a partially parsed document never yields a half-configured runtime.
A failed or partial migration never replaces the operator's source file.
Scenario cancellation still runs teardown, and replay stays deterministic across formats.

platform_cells.note: Configuration parsing is platform-neutral; the registry scopes CAP-CONFIG-TOML-JSON and CAP-SCENARIO-YAML-JSON to all supported platforms.
The CLI and daemon TOML surfaces and the scenario CLI are native-only, because the `cli` feature is native-only.

entry_points: asupersync::lab::scenario::Scenario as a serde-derived type usable with any serde format
external_ecosystem_integration.accepted_providers: Any serde-compatible data format can deserialize `Scenario`, because the type carries only serde derives and no format-specific code. That genericity is itself a preserved property.
external_ecosystem_integration.no_reexport_note: Neither `toml` nor `serde_yaml` appears in any library public signature. The only serde-format leakage into public API is `serde_json::Error` on `Scenario::from_json` / `to_json` and `serde_json::Value` in `FaultEvent.args`, `Participant.properties`, and the runner's `to_json` methods.
external_ecosystem_integration.runtime_seam_is_clean: `RuntimeConfig` is the typed target and contains no format code, so the parse layer is already separable from the runtime seam.
external_ecosystem_integration.removal_precondition: For TOML: an owned parser must accept the full current grammar with equal-or-better spans and diagnostics, and preserve write round-trips, proved against the real config corpus and both CLI and daemon journeys. For YAML: the accepted subset must first be pinned from the live corpus by asupersync-5z2scg.5.1, then matched exactly. Until both hold: KEEP.

user_journeys.description: Operator writes a partial `[scheduler]` / `[blocking]` TOML file, loads it with `RuntimeBuilder::from_toml`, layers environment overrides, and finishes with programmatic setters, relying on file < env < programmatic precedence.
ATP operator keeps layered install and daemon configuration across standard paths, inspects where each value came from via source attribution and explain-resolution, and saves changes back to TOML.
Consumer loads a RaptorQ profile through `ConfigLoader` with `RAPTORQ_` environment overrides, using the ungated owned parser and no optional features at all.
Scenario author writes YAML, runs `lab validate`, then `lab run`, and reads a located list of validation errors when the document is wrong.
Author explores seeds and replays a failing scenario deterministically, getting the same fingerprint for the same seed.
Tooling consumes `--json` output and round-trips a `Scenario` through JSON without touching YAML.

api_surface_delta.rationale: This ADR makes no source change. Every frozen symbol lives under `asupersync::runtime`, `asupersync::cli`, `asupersync::config`, or `asupersync::lab`, not at the crate root, and the capability registry pins `api_surface_map_v1.json` by semantic hash. Note that the map's `config-reexports` selector points at the INI-style `config::` module rather than the real TOML surface; that mismatch is recorded as CFG-GAP-01 and belongs to the registry owner, not to this ADR.

supersedes.stale_text: Config formats: TOML to versioned-JSON migration decision; YAML scenario migration rules
supersedes.resolution: Framed as a migration decision. The terminal decision is additive coexistence: TOML and YAML acceptance is retained indefinitely, JSON is added alongside, and no migration away from either is authorized.

migration_policy.additive_only: JSON support is added beside TOML and YAML. No accepted document that loads today may stop loading, and no field may become mandatory.
migration_policy.coexistence: TOML for configuration and YAML for scenarios remain first-class accepted inputs indefinitely. Canonical JSON may become the preferred machine-generated output without demoting either.
migration_policy.sequencing: The accepted YAML subset (asupersync-5z2scg.5.1) and the config baseline corpus (asupersync-5z2scg.4.1) must exist before any parser replacement is even evaluable. Cross-format equivalence evidence gates the additive JSON claim.
migration_policy.docs_obligation: Any change to the frozen surface updates this artifact, docs/dependency_api_adr_registry.md, and docs/adr/dep_plan_adr_004_config_scenario_formats.md in the same commit.

rollback_policy.trigger: Any previously accepted TOML or YAML document that stops loading, any coarsened diagnostic, any precedence reordering, any lost comment or value on config write-back, any change in scenario replay fingerprints, or any narrowing of include-path or size bounds.
rollback_policy.action: Revert to the frozen surface recorded here. Because the decision is additive coexistence, rollback removes the additive JSON path rather than restoring a deleted format.
rollback_policy.verification: Re-run the focused ADR contract plus the six scenario IDs owned by the two capabilities, and re-validate the full scenario corpus.

required_evidence_classes: unit: happy path, empty document, partial document, maximum nesting and size, malformed syntax, wrong types, unknown fields, and duplicate keys for both TOML and YAML
unit: precedence across file, environment, and programmatic layers, including the file-path variant of from_toml that CFG-GAP-02 says is currently untested
property: TOML and YAML and JSON round-trip idempotence over generated configurations and scenarios
differential: cross-format equivalence proving YAML and JSON deserialize to the same Scenario, which is the gap CFG-GAP-03 names
fuzz: untrusted document parsing bounded in size, nesting, and collection count with no panic
corpus: every file in examples/scenarios, frankenlab/examples/scenarios, and tools/demos still validates, runs, and replays with unchanged fingerprints
sparse-feature: default, config-file, cli, and deterministic-mode build and test cells
downstream-consumer: frankenlab and a synthesized config consumer
real E2E: the CLI lab validate/run/replay/explore journey and the ATP layered-config operator journey, including write-back round-trip fidelity
evidence.note: Naming these owners does not assert they have run. The metamorphic coverage in src/fs_config_metamorphic_tests.rs may not be counted, per CFG-GAP-06, because it tests a mock struct behind a legacy harness feature.

cutover.note: This ADR authorizes no dependency exit. `toml` and `serde_yaml` remain the incumbent parsers. Two separate implementation campaigns own the two capabilities, so both are named as primary authorities.

adrs.no_claim_boundary: This ADR is a frozen decision and public-surface inventory only. It does not prove that the planned evidence has run, that JSON is in fact lossless with respect to the accepted TOML and YAML corpora, that the accepted YAML subset has been characterized, that config write-back preserves comments, that any owned parser could reach parity, that performance is unchanged, or that either parser dependency may be removed. It also does not certify the capability registry's source-owner rows, which CFG-GAP-01 records as incorrect for this capability.
